The baglamas is a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 321.321-6, a long-necked bowl lute played by plucking. It is smaller than the bouzouki and sounds an octave higher, usually tuned D-A-D; the top four strings are pairs in unison and the low D is a pair in octaves. The body is often hollowed from a single piece of wood or made from a gourd, and some have a back of joined staves. It is about 55 cm long and 12 cm wide, easy to carry, and can even be hidden under a coat. In Greek music it is common in the Piraeus urban style of rebetiko, where it mostly gives support to the bouzouki.
希臘巴格拉馬琴為撥弦樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs編號321.321-6: The baglamas is a plucked instrument, Hornbostel–Sachs number 321.321-6. It sounds when the vibration of the strings is resonated by the bowl-shaped body; the tuning is D-A-D, the top four strings are paired at the unison and the low D is paired at the octave, so each note sounds on two strings at once. Compared with the bouzouki it is smaller and higher, and in the Piraeus style of rebetiko it usually provides support.
